content:
Here is a simple draft work schedule and some key considerations for employing a 14-year-old in your Winterthur cafe. **Please verify local regulations first**, as employment laws for minors in Switzerland are strict. ### Simple Work Schedule Draft **Employee:** Neighbor's 14-year-old son **Business:** [Your Cafe Name] - Winterthur **Schedule:** Friday & Saturday Nights until 11:00 PM | Day | Time | Tasks & Responsibilities | |-------------|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | **Friday** | 5:00 PM – 11:00 PM | • Assisting with clearing tables and wiping surfaces when directed.
• Helping with simple prep (e.g., prepping ingredients, assembling sandwiches or salads under supervision)
• Assisting with restocking non-hazardous items (e.g., sugar packets, napkins)
• Greeting customers and handing out menus/condiments with guidance | | **Saturday**| 5:00 PM – 11:00 PM | • Same duties as Friday.
• Assisting with taking drink orders from a set menu (under supervision).
• Helping manage waste bins and general cleanliness.
• Learning basic till procedures with close oversight | ### Important Considerations Before Finalizing 1. **Legal Compliance (Switzerland/Canton Zürich):** - **Minors (under 15/16):** Swiss labor laws heavily restrict the work of minors. A 14-year-old may have very limited permissible hours, especially for night work (up to 11 PM). Check with the local employment authority (Arbeitsinspektorat or canton Zürich office) to confirm legal limits (often restricted to daytime, limited hours per week, no hazardous work). - **Night work:** Working until 11 PM may be prohibited for 14-year-olds in Switzerland under current ordinances. Adjusting the shift earlier (e.g., until 8–9 PM) might be necessary to comply. 2. **Supervision:** - The teen must always be directly supervised by a responsible adult staff member while on site. Never left unattended. 3. **Safety:** - Ensure he knows the safety rules (fire exits, no entry into commercial kitchen without training, heavy equipment boundaries). - End time must be strictly enforced to ensure he can get home safely. 4. **Training:** - Brief him thoroughly on cafe operations, hygiene standards, and customer interactions. 5. **Parental Agreement:** - A written agreement between you, the teen, and his parents/guardians is prudent. Include: - Scope of duties - Hours and days - Compensation rate - Safety protocols - Termination clause - Parental responsibility for transport ### Simplified Agreement Template (For Discussion) > **Employment Agreement for Minor Worker** > > Between: **[Your Cafe Business Name]** ("Employer") > and: **[Teen's Name]** ("Worker"), son of **[Parents' Names]** ("Guardians") > > **Terms of Employment:** > > 🔹 **Duties:** Basic cleaning, table clearing, simple food preparation under direct supervision of a designated adult employee. No cooking on stoves or use of dangerous machinery. > 🔹 **Hours:** To be reviewed for legal compliance. For example: Fridays and Saturdays until [Confirm Legal End Time, e.g., 8:30 PM] or earlier, dependent on local authorization. > 🔹 **Days:** Friday and Saturday nights only. > 🔹 **Supervision:** Worker is to remain under the direct supervision of an adult staff member at all times. > 🔹 **Compensation:** [Insert hourly rate + any tips agreement] per hour worked. > 🔹 **Safety:** Worker agrees to follow all safety rules and wear provided non-slip footwear. Employer is responsible for a safe environment. > 🔹 **Transportation:** Guardians are responsible for transporting Worker to and from the Cafe. > 🔹 **Termination:** Either party may terminate with [X] days' written notice. > > **Disclaimer:** This schedule is subject to change based on Swiss cantonal labor laws for minors. Employer will ensure all regulations of the Canton of Zürich and the Swiss Federal Act on the Protection of Children and Juveniles are strictly followed. ### Recommendation **Step 1:** Contact the **Kanton Zürich - Arbeitsamt** or the **Arbeitsinspektorat Zürich** to confirm exactly what hours and tasks are legally permissible for a 14-year-old working nights in a food service establishment. **Step 2:** Adjust the schedule above based on legal feedback. If night work until 11 PM is not allowed, consider a daytime slot (e.g., Sunday afternoons) or shorter evening shifts. **Step 3:** Once legal is confirmed, provide the teen with a clear written outline of duties and safety rules. Would you like help tailoring this to a specific time frame if regulations mandate an earlier end time?

Here's a simple work schedule draft for the 14-year-old, keeping in mind legal requirements (which vary by country—Switzerland allows limited work for minors under certain conditions, often restricted by hours/day/week and type of work):

**Cafe Work Schedule - [Name of Teen]**
*Location: Your Winterthur Cafe*
*Period: Friday & Saturday Nights*
*Timeframe: Until 11:00 PM*

**Example Schedule (Adjust as needed based on cafe operation needs & local regulations):**

| Day         | Time          | Activity/Role                                 |
|-------------|---------------|----------------------------------------------|
| **Friday**  | 5:00 PM – 11:00 PM | Support with basic duties (e.g., wiping tables, clearing small orders when instructed, assisting with simple food prep like salads or sandwich assembly) |
| **Saturday**| 5:00 PM – 11:00 PM | Repeat Friday duties, plus potentially some light customer interaction (e.g., taking drink orders from a pre-selected menu, operating the till under supervision) |

**Important Notes for You & the Parents:**

1. **Local Labor Laws:** Check the exact regulations for child employment in **Switzerland/Zürich Canton**. Minors (under 15) generally have very restricted working hours, and 14-year-olds may have additional limits (e.g., maximum hours per day/week, restrictions on night shifts, types of work permitted). Contact the local employment office (Arbeitsinspektorat) or cantonal office for Winterthur to ensure compliance. Penalties for non-compliance exist.

2. **Supervision:** He should always be supervised by a responsible adult staff member while working.

3. **Safety & Comfort:** Ensure he finishes by 11 PM and is safely transported home each night. Discuss rest periods if he has school on weekends.

4. **Training & Clear Instructions:** Brief him thoroughly on cafe procedures, safety (kitchen boundaries, cleanliness, handling money), and what is expected of him each shift.

5. **Record Keeping:** Keep a simple log of hours worked for your records and to show compliance if questioned.

6. **Compensation:** Define the pay structure (hourly wage + any tips or percentage of food sales if applicable) clearly with the parents beforehand.

**Simplified Template for Agreement:**

> **Employment Agreement for Underage Worker**
> 
> Between: [Your Name/Business Name] ("The Cafe")
>                and: [Teen's Full Name] ("The Worker")
>                Parents/Guardians of Worker: [Parents' Names]
> 
> **Terms:**
> - **Duties:** Basic cleaning, clearing tables, simple food/item preparation as supervised.
> - **Hours:** Friday & Saturday nights only. From approximately [Start Time, e.g., 5:00 PM] until [End Time, e.g., 11:00 PM]. Total weekly hours will not exceed [Check Legal Limit, e.g., 8-10 hours depending on Swiss law].
> - **Supervision:** Must be under direct supervision of a Cafe employee at all times.
> - **Compensation:** [Insert Rate or Agreement].
> - **Safety:** Dress appropriately. Must follow all safety rules.
> - **Transportation:** Parents responsible for transporting him to/from the Cafe.
> - **Termination:** Either party may terminate with [X] day notice.

**Recommendation:** Before finalizing, please verify the exact legal restrictions for a 14-year-old working nights in a cafe specifically in *Winterthur, Switzerland*. The template above is a starting point, but legality is paramount.
